subject.title: feat: isolate native subagent skill workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw expose a permanent native `sessions_spawn.workspace` capability that changes a child session’s bootstrap workspace and restricts its skill-discovery roots across later turns?
rationale: The patch is additive but establishes a new model-facing execution contract and persisted session policy; code review alone cannot determine whether this capability belongs in the supported native subagent API.

options.title: Sponsor the isolated-workspace contract
options.body: Accept the new native-only capability after obtaining real behavior proof and reviewing the cross-turn isolation semantics.

options.title: Narrow to an internal seam first
options.body: Keep the public tool surface unchanged and introduce only the generic owner-approved runtime seam needed for a later API decision.

options.title: Defer the capability
options.body: Pause this PR until a maintainer confirms the product and security model for bounded child skill bundles.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the isolated-workspace contract
recommendation.body: Accept the new native-only capability after obtaining real behavior proof and reviewing the cross-turn isolation semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author is the only evidence-backed person connected to the proposed API and can clarify its intended contract; current-main ownership needs a separate history pass.
